why: Rule 1: an AI may select only from opponents it perceives. The shipped predicate is line of sight, widened to 'anything a banking profile could bank at' because indirect fire is that role's identity. Returning true outright restores full omniscience for every profile, including the non-banking ones the bound actually constrains. Remeasured 2026-09-01 at 2 of the 16 tests now in target-selection.test.ts, up from a declared 1, for the same reason and in the same file: 'the bound survives a REAL TICK -- the clone has to carry it' asserts this rule one tick deep, through stepInputs, where the pre-existing 'acquires only what it can SEE, for a profile that does not bank' asserts it at the direct call. Two depths of one rule, not a widened contract.
